title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 35-36
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 35 to 36 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'अच्युतः प्रथितः प्राणः प्राणदो वासवानुजः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 35 to 36 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 35 to 36.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 35 to 36** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **अच्युतः प्रथितः प्राणः प्राणदो वासवानुजः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**अच्युतः प्रथितः प्राणः प्राणदो वासवानुजः । अपांनिधिरधिष्ठानमप्रमत्तः प्रतिष्ठितः ॥** **स्कन्दः स्कन्दधरो धुर्यो वरदो वायुवाहनः । वासुदेवो बृहद्भानुरादिदेवः पुरन्दरः ॥**

He never falls, he is renowned, he gives life and is life itself. The younger brother of Indra is that God of gods. The treasure of the waters, the support of all, ever awake and firmly established. He is Skanda and the one who bears him, the carrier of every burden. The giver of boons, whose vehicle is the wind, is that God of gods. Vasudeva, great light, the first God and Purandara is he.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 35 to 36 mean?
faq.a: He never falls, he is renowned, he gives life and is life itself. The younger brother of Indra is that God of gods. The treasure of the waters, the support of all, ever awake and firmly established. He is Skanda and the one who bears him, the carrier of every burden. The giver of boons, whose vehicle is the wind, is that God of gods. Vasudeva, great light, the first God and Purandara is he.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
